101Propose h7The uniform ~1.07 rise gain across all sensors and all workloads, with unchanged transient time constants, and ambient at ~44.4-44.6C, is best explained as a die-wide thermal conductance deficit: the model's conductances (boundary and coupling) are too high by ~7% — reality conducts heat less well. Repair: scale all edge resistances up by ~1.07 (uniform conductance reduction). Model problem: global conductance error ~ -0.07 fractional (model conductance too high, i.e., model conductance/reality - 1 = +0.07).
102Propose h8Model ambient temperature is 42C but real ambient is ~44.4C: all-min readings (m2/m9/m24) sit ~2.4C above the model's all-min prediction, and the global linear fit intercept is +2.6C at zero rise, with residual noise/quantization (+-0.5C) around it. This is a model ambient error of ~+2.4C (real higher than model).
103NoteFINAL: LSQ over 6 workload-regime means (54 pts): real = 44.6 + 1.08*(model-42). Lambda=1.079, A=44.6C. m4 transient: real initial heating slope ~1.09x model, same tau, settles faster => POWER fault not conductance (conductance fault would slow tau). Two global model faults: (1) power gains all ~8% too low (real dissipation 1.08x model); (2) ambient 44.6 vs model 42 (+2.6C, beyond 1.0 uncertainty + 0.5 drift spec). Per-sensor residuals vs final fit all within +-1.0C = fidelity gap 0.56 + noise => NO sensor faults. Repair: power_gain x1.08 all 13 blocks (t_amb not editable via rc_edit; ambient error reported as model problem).
104Propose h9FINAL: Two global model faults. (1) Global power gain fault: real dissipated power is ~1.08x the model's calibrated power gains for every block (uniform rise gain 1.079 across all sensors/workloads; real transient heats ~9% faster with unchanged time constant, ruling out conductance error). Model power gain too low by ~7.4% (model/real - 1 = -0.074). (2) Ambient fault: real ambient ~44.6C vs model t_amb 42C (model too low by ~2.6C). No sensor faults: all per-sensor residuals within the 0.56C fidelity gap plus noise.

Global fit real = 45 + λ*(v0_rise), λ pooled ≈ 1.058 (nominally regime: mean residual +0.56; using m32: mean rise resid / mean rise = 4.83/41.62 = 0.116?? no — mean of per-sensor (real-model)/rise ratios). Per-sensor λ: c0 1.081, c1 1.078, c2 1.078, c3 1.010, c4 1.100, c5 1.107, c6 1.087, c7 1.031, pkg 1.012. Residuals vs λ=1.07 fit at nominal (m32 - v139-pred): c0 +0.9, c1 -1.7, c2 +0.2, c3 -1.7, c4 +2.5, c5 -1.5, c6 +0.5, c7 -2.5, pkg -1.7. c4 hot, c7 cold. Solo-core regimes (c0-solo r82: real 57 vs 62.4 → model +5.4 HIGH!). KEY: c0-solo real (m11) 57/50/54/51/52/52/51/50/49 vs factory prediction r82 62.4/52.8/56.3/52.2/53.3/52.3/52.4/51.2/51.1 → residuals: c0 -5.4, c1 -2.8, c2 -2.3, c3 -1.0, c4 -1.3, c5 -0.3, c6 -1.4, c7 0, pkg -2.1. ALL NEGATIVE → c0's local conductance is BETTER than model (real cooler than factory prediction) while global nominal shows real HOTTER than model. Contradiction resolved: this is a LATERAL/VERTICAL topology difference, not uniform scaling. c0 real coupling to neighbors/IHS is stronger than model. Leading hypothesis: model R too HIGH on c0-related edges, and c4/c5 too hot in nominal regime needs alternative explanation (maybe sensor? but slope-error spec ≤0.03 covers c4 λ=1.10 vs 1.058 = +0.04 marginal; c5 λ=1.107 vs 1.058 = +0.046 exceeds spec!).
